summary: I propose one small rotation: sell MSM (1.3%, Industrials, the same MRO sleeve as FAST) and put the proceeds plus the roughly $9 above the 10% cash buffer into INCY (about $17, 2.7% of equity), a Health Care name the Market Analyst favors with its earnings date verified. Stop review per L7: none of the 14 held positions has a tripped price stop. On the rate clauses after the 11-10 hot CPI, BND's (TLT -2.30% and IEF -1.24% from their 200-day averages, both short of the 3% trigger) and VNQ's (TLT not 3% below its 200-day, and the Market Analyst is not risk-off on real estate) have not tripped. IEF's 'yields materially higher' cannot be measured, but IEF is -0.16% over 5 days, so I read it as untripped. DPZ's guidance-cut item is still unconfirmed after nine sessions, and the News Analyst now treats it as having come to nothing. All 14 stops show 'missing' in the stop block; the PM should store numeric stops via thesis_updates (L6/L7). That does not need a trade slot. Lessons applied: L2 (INCY's date checked from the news note: reported 10-29, next 2027-02-09, no filings in the window), L3 (INCY overlaps IDXX, so Health Care goes from 8.1% to about 10.8%; MSM and FAST counted as one sleeve), L4 (INCY follows the Market Analyst's Health Care tilt and is not a diversification-only token buy; MSM's sale follows its Industrials avoid), and L6 (the INCY stop is a dollar level with its distance from the reference close).

proposals.thesis: MSM is a 1.3% position that duplicates FAST's industrial MRO exposure (L3; the Fundamentals Analyst says to treat FAST and MSM as one sleeve). Its gp_sector_pct (0.827) is the weakest of the analyst's top names, and the Market Analyst lists Industrials under 'avoid' (XLI 21d -0.25%, 63d -8.98%, 2.3% below its 200-day). The position is about +1.2% on cost and short-term either way, so the tax cost is negligible (about $0.10 of gain). The proceeds fund P2 in a favored sector. This is a consolidation, not a quality judgment: MSM is still F9 with cash flow above net income.
proposals.invalidation: Over the next 20 sessions MSM beats both SPY and INCY by more than 3 percentage points, or the Market Analyst moves Industrials from 'avoid' to 'favor'.

proposals.thesis: Rank 9 on the Fundamentals Analyst's list: F8, gp_sector_pct 0.906, CFO $1,413.5M against net income $1,286.7M, no flags, and low vol_252d (0.330) and beta (0.456; about -$0.78 on this position in a 10% market drop). Health Care is the Market Analyst's top favored sector (XLV 21d +9.82%, 18.97% above its 200-day), and this follows that tilt rather than reversing one (L4). Event risk is low per the News Analyst: reported 10-29, next earnings 2027-02-09, no filings in the window, and only small pipeline news (the Natera collaboration). It was the PM's named next candidate. Overlap (L3): IDXX is already held at 8.1%, so Health Care rises to about 10.8%. I size it at about 2.7% of equity for that reason and keep it a modest second name. Funded by P1 plus the roughly $9 above the 10% cash buffer, so cash stays near 10%.
proposals.invalidation: INCY closes at or below $110.00 (about 9.8% under the $121.89 reference close; re-anchor to the actual fill), or INCY underperforms XLV by more than 8 percentage points over a 21-trading-day window, or an 8-K reports a guidance cut or a failed pivotal trial.

holdings_review.why: Lowest-risk ballast (vol 4%). The bond reaction to the hot CPI was small (5-day -0.28% at TLT), so the hike looks mostly priced, and with tech still dragging SPY I expect BND's carry to roughly match or beat a choppy SPY over 20 sessions. This is the least confident hold.

Rank 2 on fundamentals (gp_sector_pct 1.0, CFO about 1.9x net income). The 11-05 beat, FY EPS guide raise and $250M buyback support it, and its 0.455 beta keeps it out of the tech drawdown, so I expect it to beat SPY.

F8 franchisor with CFO well above net income, beta about 0.1, and a Consumer Discretionary bucket the Market Analyst favors (XLY 21d +7.82%). The guidance-cut rumor has come to nothing, so I would buy it here.

I keep this as the one industrial MRO sleeve after selling MSM: F8, lowest-vol quality on the menu, and +5.7% on cost while XLI is flat. It holds up despite the Industrials 'avoid'. This is a marginal hold that I'd revisit if XLI keeps lagging.

Rank 5 (F8, gp_sector_pct 0.942). After the beat and raise it is in the Market Analyst's top sector, where XLV is +9.82% over 21 days. No earnings until 2027-02-01, so momentum plus sector tailwind should beat SPY. Insider sales are only a mild negative.

Intermediate Treasuries took the CPI shock with only a 0.16% 5-day dip and diversify an equity-heavy book. With the hike priced and the stop at 89.5 still about 1.7% away, I expect it to hold up versus a tech-dragged SPY. It is a low-conviction hold, like BND.

Negative beta and XLP +7.84% over 21 days, with Goldman raising its PT to $77 and no event until the 12-03 print. Defensive staples have outrun SPY this month, and I expect that to continue while tech stays weak. The staples stack is noted (L3).

F8 with CFO well above net income and beta 0.37, in a Financials bucket the Market Analyst favors (XLF 21d +5.89%). It reported cleanly and the next date is 2027-01-27, so I expect it to beat a tech-led SPY.

It duplicates FAST's MRO exposure in a sector the Market Analyst avoids, its profitability is the weakest of the held quality names, and at 1.3% it adds nothing FAST doesn't. I expect it to lag SPY. Matching proposal P1.

The Market Analyst's strongest sleeve (21d +6.26%, 3.82% above its 200-day, beta 0.32). The rate risk is real after CPI, but its stop at $92 is about 5% away and its clause is untripped, so I expect it to beat SPY while breadth leads cap-weight.

This is the core sleeve and by construction it tracks SPY, so I expect it to match rather than beat. I hold it because the regime is on (SPY 2.97% above the 200-day the filter computes) and the Market Analyst's lean is risk-on, so it is the right default for this money.
Like VOO, but with a small-cap and mid-cap tilt (IWM 21d +0.96% versus SPY -3.62%) and less mega-cap tech weight. That gives it a slight edge over SPY while the selling stays concentrated in tech.

Rank 1 on fundamentals (F9, gp_sector_pct 0.993) with beta about 0.05. Its Technology bucket has nothing to do with the AI-capex selloff driving XLK, so I expect it to keep beating SPY. It is +5.4% on cost while XLK is -14% over 21 days.

Five PT raises in three sessions, XLP strength and near-zero beta support it into the approximate 11-19 print. The bar is high, so the print is the main risk, but I would still buy at this price and expect it to beat SPY.
